Jensen Huang on what this actually does:

"Frontier models are the brains. BioNeMo is the scientific toolbox. Together, they give AI agents the skills of a PhD research assistant and the speed of a supercomputer."

What the toolkit enables AI agents to do right now:

Virtual drug screening: compress screening timelines from days to minutes by generating and docking compounds automatically.

Genomic analysis: transform raw sequencing data into prioritized genetic targets.

Protein design: design and validate candidates computationally before lab work begins.

Medical imaging: process and reason over imaging data to accelerate biomarker discovery.

The University of Washington's Institute for Protein Design is already using it to run RosettaFold3 at 2x faster performance than the prior generation.

I wanted to see how you’d have done holding the AI buildout for a year. So I took five representative names from each layer, plus power, and pulled the one-year return.

Turns out not every theme is created equal. It mattered far more which layer you were in than which stock you owned.

The same holds going forward, but sometimes you’re too early to feel it, and patience is the scarcest thing in this corner of the internet.

Hindsight is easy, I know. But most data points keep pointing the same way: Micron says memory supply doesn’t even start catching up until 2028, server costs are still climbing, the bottleneck just keeps moving down the stack. This buildout has years left in it.

So find the right theme, back the people telling you how things actually are, not how they wish they were, and size up.

Bears might get their week. I’d rather be positioned for the next five years.

mentions.text:
$SNOW is a great example of AI benefiting both the builders and the beneficiaries.

Revenue came in at $1.55B, up 35%, against $1.48B expected. EPS was $0.62 against $0.45. Product revenue hit $1.49B, up 37%, and that's now three straight quarters of acceleration after they ended last year at 30%.

Management says AI products drove about half of that pickup.

Q3 product revenue guided to $1.59B against $1.50B consensus, and they took the full year up to $6.07B from $5.84B in May, so 36% growth. Operating margin guidance went to 14.5% from 13.5%, and they expanded margins 400bps while growth was accelerating.

Net revenue retention at 126%. Net loss narrowed to $191.7M from $297.9M.

Growing faster and making more money at the same time is the combination nobody gets, which is why the stock is up 22% after hours.

Not everything is rosy though.

Product gross margin guidance got cut to 74% because of AI workload mix. AI revenue is compute-heavy and costs more to serve, so even the winners give something back on margin. That's the builders getting paid, and it comes straight out of the beneficiary's gross line.

And RPO grew 30% while product revenue grew 37%, so the backlog is growing slower than the business.
